result.summary: This PR modifies BCLog::LogEscapeMessage to escape newline characters (as \x0a) along with other control characters, preventing untrusted input (such as rejected RPC method names or wallet names) from spoofing log lines. It adds a util::SplitLines helper and applies it to existing intentional multiline log calls so legitimate multi-line messages remain readable across separate log entries.
result.problem: Unauthenticated or restricted RPC callers and wallet creators can supply strings containing newlines that are logged verbatim, allowing attackers to forge arbitrary log lines (like ConnectBlock errors or fake security warnings) that mislead log parsers and node operators.

resolved_concerns: Initial versions used per-subsystem string sanitization; reviewers (ryanofsky, maflcko, davidgumberg) recommended escaping newlines centrally in BCLog::LogEscapeMessage.
Wallet name validation was separated out to leave name restrictions to PR #35768, keeping this PR strictly focused on logging.

result.card: This PR fixes a log injection vulnerability where newlines in untrusted inputs (such as rejected RPC method names or wallet names) could create fake log lines in debug.log. It escapes newlines as \x0a inside the central BCLog::LogEscapeMessage helper while preserving intentional multiline messages using a new SplitLines utility. The approach has strong reviewer consensus over earlier per-subsystem string sanitizing attempts. It is ready for review and merges cleanly.
